info.title: Video Assets Server API
info.summary: One search API for free stock video: b-roll, backgrounds, nature, cities, space and archive films, with licence verdicts.
info.description:
Search 23 video sites at once (NASA, NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio, Wikimedia Commons, Internet Archive,
and deep links into Pexels, Pixabay, Shutterstock and more), get each clip's licence with a plain verdict on commercial use,
watch it, and download the rendition you need with its credits. **No video passes through this server:** posters and previews
load from the sources, and downloads are redirects to the file on the source's CDN.

**Typical flow:** `GET /v1/search` → `GET /v1/clips/{id}` → `GET /v1/clips/{id}/download?height=1080`. To cut a b-roll
sequence from a shot list in one call, `POST /v1/sequences`.

**Licence verdicts:** every clip's `license.verdict` answers "can this go into a video I publish commercially?": `yes` (commercial use ok), `yes-with-credit` (commercial use ok with credit), `restricted` (restricted: read the conditions), `clearance-required` (needs a paid licence or releases), `check-terms` (unclear: check the terms), `no` (non-commercial only).
`license.editorial=true` means people, insignia or brands appear without releases (fine for news and documentary, not for ads).
`commercial=true` keeps only `yes` and `yes-with-credit`. Verdicts are a summary, not legal advice: read the licence before publishing.

**Authentication:** the public server at video.shep.bot is open. Self-hosted servers can require a key
(`VIDEO_SERVER_API_KEY`); send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key: <key>`. Keys are accepted in headers
only, never in the URL, so they stay out of logs, browser history and Referer headers.

**For AI agents:** the same capabilities are exposed as MCP tools at `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP).
See [Use with coding agents](/docs/mcp).

**Rate limits:** 120 requests per minute per client on `/v1/*` and `/mcp`. Every response carries
`RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` (IETF RateLimit header fields) plus `RateLimit-Limit`,
`RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`; a `429` adds `Retry-After` (seconds).

**Versioning:** the major version is in the path (`/v1`). Breaking changes only ship in a new major
version; deprecated endpoints announce themselves with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers at least
90 days ahead. See [Versioning & deprecation](/docs/api/versioning).

bearer.description: Only when the server sets VIDEO_SERVER_API_KEY.

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Same key, as a header. Query parameters are not accepted.

RateLimit.description: Current quota, e.g. `"default";r=117;t=42` (r = requests remaining, t = seconds until reset).

RateLimit-Policy.description: Quota policy, e.g. `"default";q=120;w=60` (q = requests per window, w = window seconds).

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

X-License.description: The clip's licence id and verdict, e.g. `CC-BY-4.0; verdict=yes-with-credit; editorial`.

X-Attribution.description: The credit line to publish with your video (ASCII), when the licence asks for one.

example.error: Rate limit exceeded: 120 requests per 60s. Retry after 12s.

Category.description: Dot-path category; a parent (`nature`) matches its children (`nature.ocean`).

CommercialVerdict.description: Can this go into a commercially published video? `yes` (commercial use ok), `yes-with-credit` (commercial use ok with credit), `restricted` (restricted: read the conditions), `clearance-required` (needs a paid licence or releases), `check-terms` (unclear: check the terms), `no` (non-commercial only).

id.description: SPDX id where one exists (CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0…), else LicenseRef-*.

redistribution.description: May the clip itself be re-uploaded or passed on?

editorial.description: People, insignia or brands without releases: fine for news and documentary, not for ads.

assertedBy.description: `uploader` = an unverified claim (verdict capped at check-terms).

url.description: The clip's page on the source site.

width.description: Frame width of the best version.

year.description: Year the footage was made (archive films).

posterUrl.description: Still frame, on the source's CDN.

previewUrl.description: Small playable version (mp4/webm) on the source's CDN.

attribution.description: Ready-to-paste credit line when the licence asks for one.

format.description: Container: mp4, webm, mov, ogv, mpeg… (Commons originals are WebM/Ogg, never MP4).

watch.description: What a browser player should stream (straight from the source): mp4/webm near 720p.

status.description: `link` = the source can only be searched on its own site: open `searchUrl`.

query.description: The words searched after the filters were parsed out.

access.description: `api` official API; `static` a curated manifest filtered locally; `scrape` public pages; `link` deep links only (paid/partner API, no key yet, or terms that forbid aggregation).

apiKeyEnv.description: Environment variable holding the source's API key on a self-hosted server.

nativeFilters.description: Filters the source applies itself; the rest are applied locally.

oneOf.description: One shot per line; `(3s)` at the end sets that shot's length.

totalDuration.description: Seconds, split over shots without their own length (default 4 s each).

inSec.description: In-point in the source clip (skips title cards on long films).

exports.description: File contents, ready to save: an OpenTimelineIO timeline, an ffmpeg render script, a Remotion clip list and the credits. Media URLs point at the sources.

atLeast.description: The count is a lower bound.

license.description: The source's single licence id, when uniform.

total.description: Listings on the source (free and paid).

byCategory.description: Listings per top-level category; each listing counts once.

categories.description: The source's own categories or tags (may overlap).

downloads.description: Total downloads, when the source publishes them.

byCategory.description: Listings per top-level category across sources.

clients.description: Searches by client family (claude-code, cursor, browser, curl…).

assetTypes.description: Searches by category filter (`any` = no filter).

providers.description: Per-source health over the last 24 hours.

url.description: The clip's page on the source, when the file must be fetched there.

get.description: Fans out to every enabled source in parallel (each with its own timeout), then merges and ranks. Words like `4k`, `1080p`, `vertical`, `9:16`, `10s`, `under 30 seconds`, `60fps`, `timelapse` in `q` become filters (see `filters` in the response); explicit parameters win. A single length (`10s`) means at least that long. Unknown orientation, resolution, length or fps stay in the list, ranked below known matches, unless `strict=true`. A slow or failing source never fails the search: it shows up in `providers` with its status.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Short query, written like an editor would.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Comma-separated categories; a parent includes its children. Top level: nature, city, people, aerial, space, science, tech, transport, food, background, overlay, greenscreen, archive, other; children like `nature.ocean`, `city.skyline`, `space.launch`, `overlay.light`.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: Comma-separated styles (ranked first; filtered only with strict=true): timelapse, slow-motion, loop, animation, visualization, black-white.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: Comma-separated: landscape, portrait, square.

parameters.name: min_resolution
parameters.description: Short side at least: 720, 1080, 1440, 2160, or hd / fhd / 4k.

parameters.name: min_duration
parameters.description: Minimum length in seconds.

parameters.name: max_duration
parameters.description: Maximum length in seconds.

parameters.name: min_fps
parameters.description: Minimum frame rate.

parameters.name: audio
parameters.description: Only clips with (true) or without (false) a sound track.

parameters.name: commercial
parameters.description: Only clips whose licence verdict is `yes` or `yes-with-credit`.

parameters.name: free
parameters.description: Only free clips.

parameters.name: downloadable
parameters.description: Only clips with direct file links.

parameters.name: strict
parameters.description: Drop clips whose orientation, resolution, length, fps or audio is unknown when that filter is set.

parameters.name: providers
parameters.description: Comma-separated source ids (see /v1/providers).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max results (default 24).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Per-source offset for paging (e.g. 24 for page 2).

200.description: Ranked results, the filters in force and a per-source report.

400.description: Invalid parameters or unknown source id.

example.error: ✖ min_resolution must be 720, 1080, 1440, 2160 or hd/fhd/4k, got "8k"

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Clip id `<provider>:<nativeId>` (URL-encode it: ids can contain spaces and slashes).

501.description: The source has no detail pages here; open `url` on the source site.

get.description: The best file for a resolution and container (the master by default), or every file with `all=true`, with sizes and the licence.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Clip id `<provider>:<nativeId>` (URL-encode it: ids can contain spaces and slashes).

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Wanted resolution as the short side in pixels (720, 1080, 2160): the smallest file at or above it, else the biggest below.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Preferred container: mp4, webm, mov, ogv.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Only files with this role: original, rendition, preview, poster, captions.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Every file, including posters and captions.

get.description: Answers 302 to the chosen file on the source's CDN: the video never passes through this server. `height` picks a rendition (the smallest at or above it), `format` a container. The licence and credit line come back as `X-License` and `X-Attribution` headers; get the credits as files from `/v1/clips/{id}/credits`.

example.error: This clip has no direct download here; get it from the source page.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Clip id `<provider>:<nativeId>` (URL-encode it: ids can contain spaces and slashes).

post.summary: Plan a b-roll sequence from a shot list
post.description: One clip per shot, matching the target orientation, at least 1080p where possible, long enough for its shot, commercial-safe by default and directly downloadable; alternatives per shot. Returns the plan and the files to save: an OpenTimelineIO timeline, an ffmpeg script that renders the sequence, a Remotion clip list and the credits.

get.description: Every clip site with the categories it carries, pricing, licence, the filters it applies itself and whether files can be downloaded directly.

How many clips every source holds, counted once a day: listings per source, by top-level category, licence and the source's own categories, free counts, listings added in the last 30 days, and highlights such as the most downloaded clip. `atLeast: true` marks lower bounds (sources that cap their counts). Sources whose count failed today keep their last good numbers with `stale`. The same file is at `/catalog.json`; one point per day is in `/catalog-history.json`.

404.description: The census has not been built on this server.

get.description: Aggregate usage of this server: searches by surface (web, API, MCP), downloads, MCP tool calls, the client families and categories searched most, and per-source health (success rate, p50/p95 latency). Counts come from Prometheus (`source: prometheus`, last 24 hours and 7 days) or, when it is unavailable, from this process since it started (`source: process`). No queries, IPs or user agents are exposed. Cached for 60 seconds.

post.description: Stateless Model Context Protocol endpoint for AI agents. Tools: `search_videos`, `get_video`, `build_sequence`, `list_sources` (and `download_video` on local installs, which saves files with their credits). Point any MCP client at this URL; see /docs/mcp for per-client setup.
